nl: Start tools/service.py bench-service-2 8101 in the background, wait until logs/service.log contains the line ready, run tools/client.py, and finally stop the service by creating the file run/stop and waiting until the log contains the line stopped.

entries.content_utf8:
import pathlib

port = pathlib.Path("run/port").read_text()
pathlib.Path("out").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
pathlib.Path("out/response.txt").write_text(f"connected to port {port}\n")

import pathlib
import sys
import time

pathlib.Path("run").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
pathlib.Path("logs").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
time.sleep(0.5)
pathlib.Path("run/port").write_text(sys.argv[2])
with open("logs/service.log", "a") as log:
    log.write("ready\n")
while not pathlib.Path("run/stop").exists():
    time.sleep(0.1)
with open("logs/service.log", "a") as log:
    log.write("stopped\n")

oracle_program:
run ["python3", "tools/service.py", "bench-service-2", "8101"] background: true
jobs "j1" wait: 10s filter: "ready"
run ["python3", "tools/client.py"]
create "run/stop" type: file
jobs "j1" wait: 10s
reference_bash:
nohup python3 tools/service.py bench-service-2 8101 > /dev/null 2>&1 &
until grep -qx ready logs/service.log 2>/dev/null; do sleep 0.1; done
python3 tools/client.py
touch run/stop
until grep -qx stopped logs/service.log; do sleep 0.1; done
sleep 0.3
